stem: An adolescent is being reviewed because a parent says they are unsure whether his development has always progressed normally; which history element is most appropriate to include in a structured assessment?

options.text: A detailed past medical history that includes developmental progress
A single current height measurement without prior context

explanation: A detailed past medical history that includes developmental progress is the best answer. This is because developmental milestones and progress over time are essential parts of a structured paediatric history and help identify whether development has been typical or delayed.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 94

optionExplanations.A: Correct because developmental milestones and progress over time are essential parts of a structured paediatric history and help identify whether development has been typical or delayed.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because school attendance alone is too narrow and does not assess developmental progress over time.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a single height measurement provides only a snapshot and does not address developmental history.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because dietary history may be relevant, but on its own it does not review developmental progress.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because pubertal assessment is useful, but it does not replace a developmental history.
